To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
information security education is a process, information security training is a method of delivering information security education, and information security training is an event.
the three concepts (namely information security education, training and awareness) are different in terms their focus, purpose, and method of delivery.

(1) the focus of information security education is on knowledge, skills and abilities; the focus of information training is on knowledge and skills; and the focus of information awareness is on knowledge; (2) the purpose of information security education and information security training is to change behaviour, whereas the purpose of information awareness is to increase knowledge; and (3) the method of delivery of information security education involves a formal educational approach, the method of delivery for information security training is formal or informal training,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conceptual analysis of these three important information security concepts and their relationship to each other.
the conceptual analysis of information education, information security awareness, and information security training.
providing a clear distinction between information security education and training and information security training and awareness, and to provide a working definition for each concept.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

information security training is more focused and more specific than information security education and that information security awareness is less focused and less specific than information security training.

information security education is a long-term, continuous, formal process of imparting information security knowledge and skills to individuals, whereas information security training is a short-term, formal and informal process of imparting specific information security knowledge and information security skills to individuals.

information security training focuses on the development of technical skills; information security education focuses on developing the ability to understand the concepts, theories, principles and methods of information security; and information security awareness focuses on developing a general understanding of the organisation’s information security policies and procedures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
information security awareness is a broad term which includes information security education and information security training.
information security education, training and awareness are different and should be used at different stages of an organisation’s information security lifecycle.
information security education is a long-term process of developing information security skills, knowledge and attitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

information security training is a subset of information security education and that information security awareness is a subset of both information security education and information security training.

organisations can use these definitions to determine the appropriate information security training and education programme for their organisation and the information security awareness programme to introduce to their organisation.
information security education, training and awareness are different concepts, but they are inter-related.
